items.title: Section: The Fourth Yogic Process Opens — Two Paths From Near-Attainment Concentration

items.zh: 復次，此嗢拕南曰：七作意離欲、及諸定、廣辯、二定、五神通、生差別、諸相。觀察於諸諦，如實而通達，廣分別於修，究竟為其後。
items.en: Within the Basic Section, in the Ground of the Hearer-Disciples, the first part of the fourth yogic process. Further, the summary verse says: "Seven mental engagements free one from desire, and the absorptions are explained at length; two attainments, five superknowledges, and the differentiated marks of rebirth." "Investigating the truths, one penetrates them as they truly are; the varieties of cultivation are explained at length, culminating, at the very end, in the ultimate fruit."

items.zh: 已得作意諸瑜伽師，已入如是少分樂斷；從此已後，唯有二趣，更無所餘。
items.en: A yoga practitioner who has attained mental engagement has already entered this partial delight in severing affliction. From this point on, there are exactly two paths open, and no others.

items.zh: 何等為二？一者、世間，二、出世間。彼初修業諸瑜伽師，由此作意，或念我當往世間趣，或念我當往出世趣。復多修習如是作意。如如於此極多修習，如是如是所有輕安、心一境性，經歷彼彼日夜等位，轉復增廣。若此作意堅固、相續、強盛而轉，發起清淨所緣勝解，於奢摩他品及毘鉢舍那品，善取其相。彼於爾時，或樂往世間道發起加行，或樂往出世道發起加行。問：此中幾種補特伽羅，即於現法樂往世間道發起加行，非出世道？

items.title: Section: Four Kinds of Practitioner Who Choose the Mundane Path

items.zh: 答：略有四種補特伽羅。何等為四？一、一切外道；二、於正法中根性羸劣，先修止行；三、根性雖利，善根未熟；四、一切菩薩樂當來世證大菩提，非於現法。如是四種補特伽羅，於現法中，樂往世間道發起加行。
items.en: Answer: There are, in brief, four kinds of person. What are the four? First, every follower of an outside path. Second, one within the true teaching whose faculties are weak, who first cultivates correct conduct accordingly. Third, one whose faculties are sharp, but whose wholesome roots are not yet ripe. Fourth, every bodhisattva who wishes to realise great enlightenment in a future life, not in this present life. These four kinds of person, in this present life, delight in applying effort towards the mundane path.

items.zh: 此樂往世間道發起加行者，復有二種。一者、具縛，謂諸異生；二、不具縛，謂諸有學。此復云何？

items.title: The Six-Aspect Method: Coarse Below, Peaceful Above

items.zh: 謂先於欲界觀為麁性，於初靜慮若定、若生觀為靜性，發起加行，離欲界欲；如是乃至發起加行，離無所有處欲，當知亦爾。
items.en: That is, one first observes the desire realm as coarse, and observes the first dhyāna — whether the concentration itself or the resulting rebirth there — as peaceful; applying effort in this way, one becomes free of desire for the desire realm. In just this way, applying effort onward, one becomes free of desire even for the sphere of nothingness — this should be understood identically at every stage.

items.title: Section: What the Mundane Path Yields — Attainments Without Mind, Five Superknowledges, and Heavenly Rebirth

items.zh: 又依靜慮等，能引無想定等及發五神通等。又即依此若生、若相，皆當廣說。
items.en: Further, relying on the dhyānas and so on, one is able to give rise to the attainment of non-perception and the like, and to develop the five superknowledges and so on. And, relying on these same attainments, both the resulting rebirth and the marks of freedom from desire shall all be explained at length.

items.title: Section: The Seven Kinds of Mental Engagement Named

items.zh: 為離欲界欲，勤修觀行諸瑜伽師，由七作意方能獲得離欲界欲。何等名為七種作意？謂了相作意、勝解作意、遠離作意、攝樂作意、觀察作意、加行究竟作意、加行究竟果作意。
items.en: For a yoga practitioner diligently cultivating contemplation in order to become free of desire for the desire realm, it is through seven kinds of mental engagement that freedom from desire for the desire realm is actually attained. What are these seven kinds of mental engagement? Learning the object's mark, confident understanding, seclusion, gathering joy, examination, the culmination of effort, and the fruit of that culmination.

items.title: Section: Learning the Object's Mark Opens — the Meaning and Substance of Desire's Coarseness

items.zh: 云何名為了相作意？謂若作意，能正覺了欲界麁相，初靜慮靜相。云何覺了欲界麁相？謂正尋思欲界六事。何等為六？一、義，二、事，三、相，四、品，五、時，六、理。
items.en: What is called learning the object's mark? It is the mental engagement able to correctly recognise the desire realm's coarse mark and the first dhyāna's peaceful mark. How does one recognise the desire realm's coarse mark? By rightly investigating six things regarding the desire realm: meaning, substance, characteristic, category, time, and principle.

items.zh: 謂正尋思：如是諸欲有多過患、有多損惱、有多疫癘、有多災害。於諸欲中多過患義，廣說乃至多災害義，是名麁義。云何尋思諸欲麁事？謂正尋思：於諸欲中有內貪欲，於諸欲中有外貪欲。
items.en: One rightly investigates: these desires carry much danger, much distress, much disease, and much calamity. Investigating desire's much danger, and so on at length through its much calamity — this is called the meaning of its coarseness. One rightly investigates: within these desires there is inner craving, and within these desires there is outer craving.

items.title: Section: Desire's Particular Characteristics — Object-Desire, Affliction-Desire, and Three Kinds of Distortion

items.zh: 謂正尋思：此為煩惱欲，此為事欲。此復三種。謂順樂受處、順苦受處、順不苦不樂受處。順樂受處是貪欲依處，是想、心倒依處；順苦受處是瞋恚依處，是忿、恨依處；順不苦不樂受處是愚癡依處，是覆、惱、誑、諂、無慚、無愧依處，是見倒依處。
items.en: One rightly investigates: this is affliction-desire, this is object-desire. Object-desire is further threefold: what conduces to pleasant feeling, what conduces to painful feeling, and what conduces to neutral feeling. What conduces to pleasant feeling is the basis for craving, and the basis for distorted perception and distorted mind. What conduces to painful feeling is the basis for hatred, and the basis for indignation and resentment. What conduces to neutral feeling is the basis for delusion, and the basis for concealment, irritability, deceit, flattery, shamelessness, and lack of conscience — and the basis for distorted view.

items.zh: 即正尋思：如是諸欲，極惡諸受之所隨逐，極惡煩惱之所隨逐。是名尋思諸欲自相。
items.en: One then rightly investigates: these desires are pursued by the most severe kinds of feeling, and pursued by the most severe afflictions. This is called investigating the particular characteristic of desire.

items.title: Desire's Universal Characteristics: Suffering and Impermanence

items.zh: 謂正尋思：此一切欲，生苦、老苦，廣說乃至求不得苦等所隨逐、等所隨縛。諸受欲者，於圓滿欲驅迫而轉，亦未解脫生等法故，雖彼諸欲勝妙圓滿，而暫時有。是名尋思諸欲共相。
items.en: One rightly investigates: all these desires are pursued and bound by the suffering of birth, the suffering of old age, and so on at length through the suffering of not obtaining what is sought. Those who indulge in desire are driven and compelled in pursuit of ever more complete satisfaction, never freed from birth and the rest — so that even the most excellent, complete desires, however fine, are only ever temporary. This is called investigating the universal characteristic of desire.

blocks.text: Fascicle 33 opens the **fourth yogic process**: how a practitioner who has reached the preparatory concentration goes on, by the mundane or supramundane path. Today: the two paths, and the **seven attentions** (七種作意) by which one becomes free of desire. A passage (0465b05) is untranslated.

After attaining "mental engagement" (Day 282), "there are exactly two paths, and no others": the mundane and the supramundane. The untranslated prose: as the practitioner cultivates this attention, pliancy and one-pointedness grow day by day, and one comes to delight in setting out on one path or the other.

Four kinds of people: followers of other paths; those in the Buddha's teaching whose faculties are weak; those with sharp faculties whose wholesome roots are not yet ripe; and "every bodhisattva who wishes to realise great awakening in a future life, not this one". Master Cháng Bǎi: for others, progress means absorption.
"One observes the desire realm as coarse and the first absorption as peaceful", and so on up to the sphere of nothingness. Master Cháng Bǎi: this temporarily suppresses affliction.
Learning the mark; confident understanding; seclusion; gathering joy; examination; the culmination of effort; and its fruit.

One recognises the desire realm's coarseness through the six things. **Meaning**: "much danger, much distress, much disease, much calamity". **Substance**: inner and outer craving. **Own mark**: affliction-desire and object-desire; objects conducing to pleasant, painful, or neutral feeling are the bases of craving, hatred, and delusion. **Shared mark**: all desires are pursued by the sufferings of birth, ageing, and the rest, and are impermanent.

quiz.q: One with mental engagement has "exactly two paths, no others." What does Master Cháng Bǎi say?
options: after access concentration there are two directions — no third
quiz.why: "From this point on, there are exactly two paths open, and no others." Master Cháng Bǎi: after attaining access concentration there are two directions to go — no third road.

quiz.q: The first of the four is every outside-path follower. Why, according to Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: they take absorption as progress, even mistaking it for nirvāṇa
quiz.why: "First, every follower of an outside path." Master Cháng Bǎi: for outsiders, progress means attaining absorption — they even regard absorption as nirvāṇa — so all outsiders train by the mundane path.

quiz.q: Fourth, bodhisattvas who wish for awakening in a future life also take the mundane path. How do the masters view their absorption and powers?
options: both: powers inspire faith, but real liberation comes through the Dharma
quiz.why: "Fourth, every bodhisattva who wishes to realise great enlightenment in a future life, not in this present life." Venerable Miào Jìng: displaying powers makes beings readily faithful and glad; but what truly liberates them is the Dharma. Master Cháng Bǎi: using powers to guide beings isn't ultimate, but helps them give rise to faith.

quiz.q: How far does the mundane path's freedom from desire go, according to Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: only temporarily suppressing active affliction, not cutting its seeds
quiz.why: "One first observes the desire realm as coarse." Master Cháng Bǎi: the mundane path temporarily suppresses active affliction; it doesn't cut the seeds.

quiz.q: What are the seven engagements, and how does Master Cháng Bǎi explain seclusion?
options: the seven; seclusion first abandons the lower stage's uppermost coarse afflictions
quiz.why: "Learning the object's mark, confident understanding, seclusion, gathering joy, examination, the culmination of effort, and the fruit of that culmination." Master Cháng Bǎi: third, seclusion — the engagement that first abandons all the lower stage's uppermost, coarse afflictions.

quiz.q: Desires carry "much disease." What example does Master Cháng Bǎi give?
options: gluttony causing gastritis — desire underlies much illness
quiz.why: "These desires carry much danger, much distress, much disease, and much calamity." Master Cháng Bǎi: for instance, gluttony brings gastritis and the like — desire is the basis of many diseases.

quiz.q: "This is affliction-desire, this is object-desire." How does Master Cháng Bǎi distinguish them?
options: the grasping mind is affliction-desire; the grasped object is object-desire
quiz.why: "This is affliction-desire, this is object-desire." Master Cháng Bǎi: in terms of the cognizing mind, it is affliction-desire; in terms of the cognized object, it is object-desire.
